abstract: Due to occlusions, variable head positions, face deformations, and motion blur under unconstrained situations, facial expression recognition (FER) in the wild is exceedingly difficult. Previous studies were mostly developed for laboratory-controlled FER, despite significant development in automated FER over the last few decades. Real-world occlusions, varied head positions, and other difficulties significantly raise the difficulty of FER due to these poorly informed regions and complicated backdrops. Unlike prior exclusively CNN-based approaches, we think that converting face pictures into visual word sequences and performing global expression recognition is viable and practicable. As a result, we develop Attention Fusion Transformer (AF-Transformer) as a two-step solution to FER in the wild. To begin, we suggest using Attention Fusion (AF) to combine two feature maps produced by a dual-branch CNN. By combining numerous characteristics with global-local attention, AF collects discriminative information. Flattening and projecting the fused feature maps into visual word sequences follows. Second, we suggest modelling the link between these visual words and global self-attention, inspired by the success of Transformers in natural language processing. Three publicly available in-the-wild facial expression datasets are used to test the suggested approach. Extensive studies show that our technique outperforms other methods in the same context.

articleTitle: Deterministic bounds on performance about software defined network based on network calculus
publicationTitle: 2022 3rd International Conference on Computer Vision, Image and Deep Learning & International Conference on Computer Engineering and Applications (CVIDL & ICCEA)
abstract: When the SDN controller sends flow table entries to all switches in the routing path, aiming at the flow table miss caused by the flow table timeout mechanism, we proposed a bound analysis method of SDN performance based on network calculus. The method describes the interaction between data flows and control flows in switches and controller, and analyzes the bound of SDN performance when the data flows match or miss. Especially in the analysis of the flow table miss, we introduced the flow table timeout value and a new arrival curve which is more rigorous than the traditional affine function, then deduced the bound of network performance. Finally, Ryu and Mininet were used to simulate the end-to-end delay and backlog performance of SDN, and compared with the theoretical results of the analytical model, providing a basis for the parameter setting of SDN.

articleTitle: Differential sparse single-pixel imaging with wavelet coefficients
publicationTitle: 2022 3rd International Conference on Computer Vision, Image and Deep Learning & International Conference on Computer Engineering and Applications (CVIDL & ICCEA)
abstract: Wavelet tree-based adaptive compressed ghost imaging has higher imaging speed and better imaging quality than compressed sensing methods. However, the number of samples can be reduced, since finer significant coefficients can be calculated with the existing measurements. This paper proposes a compressive adaptive ghost imaging with block-wise computational sampling in this paper. This method takes full use of the sparsity of the image in the wavelet domain. The block-wise computational sampling computes four LL band coefficients of high resolution via fewer than two measurements. The calculation strategy takes the useful information of the sampled low-resolution coefficients. This brings in fewer measurements. The computed LL band coefficients are also used to sample significant HH, HL, and LH coefficients of the same scale. The extended prediction method can accurately locate the positions of the important coefficients, by eliminating insignificant coefficients that belongs to significant parent coefficient. The simulation results show that the proposed compressive adaptive ghost imaging using block-wise computing sampling can achieve lower rate of sampling and advanced imaging quality.

articleTitle: Scheme design of one-stop tracing service center
publicationTitle: 2022 3rd International Conference on Computer Vision, Image and Deep Learning & International Conference on Computer Engineering and Applications (CVIDL & ICCEA)
abstract: The one-stop tracking service platform is a production and marketing service center established in a completely decentralized network environment. Based on scattered enterprise information applications, it provides enterprises with a complete set of PAAS platform solutions of cloud application development platform and cloud application governance platform through container technology and micro service architecture
